_notes: FIRST RECIPE TO USE `sources` -- two sheets, not one, because the delivery
itself was two sheets: a travelling ball with nothing to say about impact,
and a contact burst with nothing to say about flight. Splitting a single
sequence across them is the honest read of README.md's own suggested
assembly ("stop the core at contact and play the contact sequence once").
DELIVERED WITH ITS OWN ALPHA (measured: 0% opaque-black pixels sampled
across all four PNGs), so keyed is false and nothing is re-keyed from
luminance -- see the sources' own README for the generation note.
THE 443/444 ALTERNATION IS ACCEPTED, NOT FIXED. water_contact_8f.png is
1774x887 over a 4x2 grid: 1774/4 and 887/2 are not integers, so the slicer
truncates each cell by up to a pixel and warns. The README's own column
edges (0, 444, 887, 1331, 1774) already alternate 444/443/444/443 for
exactly this reason -- a uniform floor-divided grid loses at most one row
or column of edge pixels per cell, which is nothing against a 512-padded
canvas.
TWO DIFFERENT CELL SIZES, ONE SHARED CANVAS. The core's cells are 512x512;
the contact cells truncate to 443x443/444x444. pad_to_common_canvas centres
every contact cell, transparent-padded, onto 512x512 so the sequence never
changes box size frame to frame -- SpellVfxPlayer fits the whole sequence
into one box and a mid-flight resize would be the tell.
SIX FRAMES OF FLIGHT, STRAIGHT THROUGH. water_core_6f.png is already an
authored six-frame loop of internal motion -- nothing to compose, the cells
ARE the frames, in order.
CONTACT: ALL EIGHT CELLS, ONE HELD. Looked hard at whether contact_f0 (the
compact ball with spray just starting) duplicates the last flight frame
closely enough to cut -- it does not: core_f5 has one unbroken comet tail,
contact_f0 has that tail already fragmenting into the first loose droplets.
Cutting it would jump straight from a smooth ball to a squash-in-progress
with nothing bridging them, which reads worse than one extra frame that is
merely similar rather than identical. Kept.
contact_f0 SCALED UP 1.10x, and this is a measured correction, not a look:
the two sheets do not draw the ball at the same size in its own cell --
core_f5's content bbox is 454x472 of 512, contact_f0's is 425x417 of 444,
a 7-13% gap wide enough that the ball visibly shrank for one frame right
before impact when composed straight. 1.10 splits the two axes' ratios
(1.068 / 1.132); scaled about the cell's own centre, same mechanism
frost_flare's wind-up and mud_burst's held impact already use.
contact_f3 is the peak -- 27% coverage against the runner-up's 23%, and the
widest crown in the sheet by eye -- so it gets hold: 2, the second 6%
larger, the same trick frost_flare and mud_burst use for a landed blow:
one frame reads as a drawing going past, two growing into each other reads
as impact. No pivot stated: the crown is drawn centred in its own cell, so
growing about the cell's own centre is right without saying so.
15 frames, flight at 6/15 = 40% of the runtime. seconds 0.65 puts each
frame at ~43ms, in the same band mud_burst and frost_flare already ship at.
